proof_summary: The identity \(k\binom{n+k-1}{k}=n\binom{n+k-1}{k-1}\) first removes the outer division, after which the sum at \(pM\) is partitioned into indices divisible and not divisible by \(p\). Reciprocal and reciprocal-square sums over reduced residue blocks have the required \(p\)-adic valuations (from unit-square cancellation and reflection), while the product factorization \(\binom{p(M+j)}{pj}=\binom{M+j}{j}\prod_{p\nmid h}(1+pM/h)\), expanded through quadratic order, shows each divisible-index term differs from its scaled counterpart by a multiple of \(p^{3r}\); the nondivisible-index sum has the same divisibility.
